source.label: Opt-in browser social post ingestion
notes: Read-only browser automation through an explicitly selected OpenCLI site session; Instagram defaults to an ephemeral session and persistent authentication is opt-in.
No likes, follows, comments, messages, saves, stars, subscriptions, profile edits, or other mutations are performed.

Instagram profile grids and X profile timelines are treated as opt-in read-only sources when explicitly targeted. Instagram adapter calls use one ephemeral site session by default; they stop on auth/challenge/rate-limit responses rather than rotating sessions.
X ingestion mode: adapter. Browser, adapter, and hybrid modes are read-only; hybrid prefers the authenticated adapter and uses the DOM only to fill incomplete results.
LinkedIn ingestion mode: hybrid. Personal /in/ profiles may use the authenticated adapter; company /company/ pages always retain DOM collection support.
Logged-in LinkedIn activity scraping is disabled unless both --platforms=linkedin and --allow-linkedin are passed. Auth and rate-limit failures open a circuit so untouched targets remain retryable.

Instagram login, challenge, and rate-limit failures open a circuit immediately; repeated command or profile failures open it after three consecutive failed targets. Legitimate empty native timelines remain completed empty checks.
Checkpoint owner-collision reconciliation: 0 stale company rows reattributed, 0 quarantined.
Each target is checkpointed independently; blocked or timed-out profiles are logged and do not stop the batch.

El anuncio se realizó en el Vertical Video Summit de Los Ángeles, un evento de la industria de video vertical, donde también participan competidores como ReelShort, DramaBox y Holiwater.
La compañía fue cofundada por Gabriela Tafur, abogada caleña con un MBA de Stanford, que ha sido también presentadora de Caracol Televisión, Señorita Colombia y cuarta finalista en Miss Universo. Su cofundador, Esteban Ramírez, cuenta con un MBA y una maestría en Ciencias de la Computación del MIT.
Los microdramas son series en formato vertical (diseñadas para verse en el celular) con episodios de entre 60 y 90 segundos y temporadas de cerca de 80 capítulos.
El formato, originado en China, generó ingresos globales de $11.000 millones de dólares en 2024, según reportes de la industria, y creció 35% ese año tras un salto de 268% en 2023. Las empresas chinas concentran actualmente el 83% de esos ingresos.
“La única parte de la industria del entretenimiento que está creciendo 200% año tras año”, explicó Tafur en entrevista con Forbes Colombia. “No ha habido disrupción en el mundo del entretenimiento desde la invención de la televisión lineal en América Latina. Ya es hora de que la industria sufra un sacudón”.
La idea nació en noviembre de 2024, cuando Tafur regresó a Colombia durante el Día de Acción de Gracias y observó que varias manicuristas consumían en sus celulares novelas chinas dobladas al español.
Desde ese momento comenzó a estructurar la compañía, que en sus primeras versiones se llamó Latido antes de renombrarse como Idilio, semanas después de aparecer en la lista Forbes 30 Under 30.
La historia completa en Forbes.co

But people seem to really love using it as an AI interface that isn't chat that can work in their program of choice. Examples of usage so far: - A Mom building her first app on Lovable - A dentist Show more Quote Farza @FarzaTV · Apr 6 I built this thing called Clicky. It's an AI teacher that lives as a buddy next to your cursor. It can see your screen, talk to you, and even point at stuff, kinda like having a real teacher next to you. @gabrielatafur Suena bonito. El problema es que la vida rara vez cabe en frases tan absolutas.
Hay personas correctas que llegan en momentos donde no hay paz, sino crecimiento.
Hay relaciones sanas que pasan días sin verse porque existen trabajo, distancia, responsabilidades o simplemente dos adultos construyendo su propio proyecto de vida.
Hay quienes son la primera llamada cuando todo sale bien...
y otros que, precisamente porque te aman, saben cuándo no deben ser el centro de tu mundo.
La persona correcta no es la que elimina el conflicto, la espera o la incertidumbre.
Es la que, incluso cuando existen, sigue eligiendo construir contigo.
Confundir comodidad con amor ha hecho que muchas personas abandonen relaciones valiosas y permanezcan en otras que solo eran cómodas.
Porque la paz no siempre es señal de amor.
A veces también es señal de costumbre.

evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2058603225859977517","author":"michaelzixizhou","name":"Michael Zhou","text":"I got into @ycombinator S26!

 The past 6 months have felt like 2 years:
 - Turned down 7-figure new grad offers at top companies
 - Bootstrapped until my bank account hit zero
 - Pivoted 5 times, and did door-to-door sales for a couple of months
 - Joined @zfellows and flew out to SF last month
 - Cancelled my return flight to Toronto
 - Had wonderful neighbours I'd just met crowd-fund my apartment deposit
 - Got the call from @aroraharshita33 6 hours after my YC interview

...all without telling my mom.

Codag is the crystallization of everything I picked up across infrastructure, systems, and platform engineering. 

Our thesis is that within two years, agents will be the primary consumer of logs, and soon the primary producer of them. Today's observability stack and dashboards were built for humans to look at. Agents are a different reader entirely, and the infrastructure for understanding systems at scale has to be rebuilt for them.

That is what we're building. We start with log compression: turning millions of lines into a compact, cited capsule an agent can actually read, so it stops drowning and starts debugging. 

I cannot believe I get to work on this full time - I wake up every day looking forward to building more. To everyone who made it real: @carterkev, @cory, @aroraharshita33, @amiklas, @nemild for taking the bet, the neighbours who backed a stranger with a laptop, and the countless friends that support me. Thank you.

We just published an open source CLI and algorithm for log compression, fully free at https://t.co/GmXKUIFTQf. If your agent debugs production, I'd love for you to try it, or just to talk. Got a lot more coming soon, and most of it will be open source.

evidence.title: 「Mirror Mirror AI 到底在做什麼？」 創業以來已經被問到不好意思的我們決定公開我們的產品了！ 除了展品介紹之外，我們也會介紹超可愛的九人團隊成員、產品開發幕後花絮、品牌客戶專訪、與fashion & AI的趨勢 追蹤我們的亞洲地區專屬帳號 @mmai.asia 讓我們與你分享我們是怎麼用AI來協助時尚產業的吧！ — “What exactly does Mirror Mirror AI do?” Since starting our company, we’ve been asked this question so many times that we finally decided it’s time to make our product public! {"id":"2039808508514971816","author":"imjennywen","name":"jenny 🍞","text":"announcement: we’re backed by @a16z @speedrun!

a few months ago, i walked away from everything and moved to san francisco.

my best friends left behind businesses, jobs, and other colleges.

all for a crazy idea:

build an AI caretaker for seniors.

the journey has been crazy. we hit 1M views on demos, received support from doctors and researchers, and we’re getting hundreds of orders from families across the US.

this started as a personal project for my grandma.

i just wanted to build a device to keep her safe.

but now, this has grown into something much bigger.

we’re ready to tackle one of the world’s most important problems:

getting seniors the care they deserve.

right now, eldercare is unaffordable and inaccessible. we’re going to fix that.

our team has the distribution ability to take eldercare hardware to the world.

we’ve generated 7-figures across previous companies, published research cited by the mayo clinic, and worked for high-growth startups and fortune 100 consumer electronics companies…

evidence.title: I got into YC twice.
evidence.text: I got into YC twice. The first time, we got acquired. Runtime (P26) is part of @ycombinator. After Mentum's acquisition, I shipped 4 full-stack products at Nuvocargo in 3 months, then enabled the rest of the team to do the same. I obsessed over making it so easy and safe that anyone can spin up an environment in milliseconds, prompt, deploy, and create PRs. At Runtime, we give teams guardrails and observability to enable anyone to ship with coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Copilot, etc.) We’re already working with YC scaleups and used in 40 countries with zero ad spend. evidence.title: 「AI 會取代時尚創作嗎？我們先來看看 100 年前的這場革命。」 從 1892 年創刊後的 40 年間，《Vogue》封面完全不准放照片。 為什麼？因為那時的人覺得攝影「沒有靈魂」。 但到了 1920 年代，為了追求更快的出刊速度與全球影響力，攝影成了唯一的選擇。 這聽起來是不是很熟悉？ 現在我們談論 AI 的恐懼、美學爭議、創作者權利，其實在攝影取代插畫的年代，早就全都上演過一遍了。 💡 你覺得 AI 是時尚的「破壞者」還是「進化推手」？ 在底下留言告訴我們你的看法！ 追蹤 @mmai.asia 看我們如何運用 AI，在致敬傳統的同時，為時尚產業提速。 “Would Vogue still be Vogue today if it had rejected photography?” Did you know that for its first 40 years, Vogue covers were exclusively illustrated? Photography was seen as ”too mechanical“ and ”not fashion enough.“ But eventually, it was the need for efficiency and scale that turned the camera into the industry’s most powerful tool. History is repeating itself. The rise of Generative AI today mirrors the photography revolution of a century ago. It’s not just about art vs. machine; it’s about an industry evolving to meet a new reality. At Mirror Mirror AI, we don‘t just watch these trends—we build them. Follow our Asia-focused account @mmai.asia and join us as we explore how AI is redefining the future of fashion. ✨

evidence.title: Nothing quite like doing everything “right” and still waking up looking three months along. Same food, same routine, a completely different body twelve hours later... love that journey for me. I tracked my sleep, my steps, my training, my blood sugar. Meanwhile the organ running the show? Never checked it once. Not a peep. Turns out most of us have never tested our gut, we just buy whatever probiotic has the prettiest label and cross our fingers. But your microbiome is unique to you, so “made for everyone” is a polite way of saying made for no one. Anyway I’ve read approximately 4,000 studies this week and I will not be recovering. What’s the one health metric you track like your life depends on it? 👇 @gutgutgoose #GutgutgoosePartner

Same food, same routine, a completely different body twelve hours later... love that journey for me. I tracked my sleep, my steps, my training, my blood sugar.

Meanwhile the organ running the show? Never checked it once. Not a peep.

Turns out most of us have never tested our gut, we just buy whatever probiotic has the prettiest label and cross our fingers. But your microbiome is unique to you, so “made for everyone” is a polite way of saying made for no one.

Anyway I’ve read approximately 4,000 studies this week and I will not be recovering.

What’s the one health metric you track like your life depends on it?

evidence.title: Звук. Зображення. Швидкість руху 💪 ⠀ Завдяки технологіям на базі ШІ дані з акустичних й оптичних сенсорів миттєво об’єднуються в єдину картину поля бою. Результат — система бачить і вираховує координати повітряної цілі майже без затримки. ⠀ У межах програми Test in Ukraine протестували рішення для виявлення FPV-дронів від американського стартапу Surtr. Результати тестування показали хорошу технологічну зрілість як для прототипу. ⠀ Розробники вже отримали фідбек від українських військових і Brave1, що допоможе їм розвинути й адаптувати систему для реального бойового застосування. Такі технології — перший крок до створення комплексів активного захисту проти дронів, що здатно кардинально змінити ситуацію на полі бою. ⠀ Дивіться у відео, як пройшли випробування.

I couldn’t be prouder of my team. We’ve been through every kind of challenge, but after experimenting and learning relentlessly, we’ve set a new direction to set the standard of how the fashion industry will adopt AI moving forward. We’re keeping the details in stealth for now, but I can confidently say this marks the next era of fashion.

Thank you to everyone who has believed in us: our angels, our advisors, our friends and family. We’re moving full speed into what’s to come next. 💫

evidence.title: Alex Hyungwoo Noh LinkedIn post
evidence.text: Robots are getting great at seeing the world. They're still terrible at touching it. The reason is data. There's an ocean of video to learn from, and almost nothing that captures what a hand actually feels - the pressure, the contact, the grip - while doing real tasks in real homes. At 6thSense, we built a wearable that captures exactly that. Every frame records what the hands see and feel: pressure across every finger, object contact, and 3D hand pose - in any kitchen, any hallway, anywhere. Not a lab. The real world. We believe this is the missing layer for teaching robots dexterity and master manipulation tasks. Excited to share that we're in YC S26!! hashtag #Robotics hashtag #Egocentric hashtag #Manipulation hashtag #YCombinator hashtag #Tactile hashtag #PhysicalAI …more

Team up on the go with other players and keep each other safe until extraction, or leave the team at any moments to betray them if they’ve pissed you off. 2⃣ Collect Gears and Relics You decide how to gather your loot: dive into intense PvP battles or keep your distance and focus on PvE, in team or solo. Just remember - Gears make you stronger, and Relics drive your progress. 3⃣ Get the F*ck Out Alive! It’s simple: either you make it out alive or you don’t - only those who extract get to keep their loot. So be careful who you trust out there, and make sure to balance your risk/reward appetite. Join the Playtests from our website, and come improve the game with the Devs. #gamedev #mobilegamedev #antihero #bestmobilegames

1⃣ Build Friendships, or Break Them.
In MISFITZ, you control the matchmaking. Team up on the go with other players and keep each other safe until extraction, or leave the team at any moments to betray them if they’ve pissed you off.

It’s simple: either you make it out alive or you don’t - only those who extract get to keep their loot. So be careful who you trust out there, and make sure to balance your risk/reward appetite.

{"id":"2078832132735320340","author":"dirtman","name":"Angus (dirtman)","text":"This post is something else man 🤣 https://t.co/KykKk0BH5Z","likes":48,"retweets":1,"replies":3,"views":2379,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Sun Jul 19 13:19:37 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/dirtman/status/2078832132735320340","has_media":true,"media_urls":["https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HNl-zmaakAEer0T.jpg"],"media_posters":["https://pbs.twimg.com/media/HNl-zmaakAEer0T.jpg"],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2078133895766114412","author":"deanwball","name":"Dean W. Ball","text":"Some observations on Kimi: 

1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run. 

2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China. 

3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "the art of not being governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex. 

4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure." This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business. 

5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this. 

6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked.","created_at":"Fri Jul 17 15:05:05 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/deanwball/status/2078133895766114412","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

As of May 2026, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) has officially been renamed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS).

The change was published following a global consensus process involving over 22,000 patients, clinicians, and researchers across 50+ medical organizations.

“Polycystic” implied the condition was defined by ovarian cysts, but you don’t need cysts to have PMOS. Many people diagnosed with it never had them. That framing narrowed the focus to the ovaries and contributed to delayed diagnosis, with up to 70% of affected individuals still undiagnosed.

In reality, PMOS is a metabolic and endocrine condition. It affects 1 in 8 women, and it operates across multiple systems at once. The new name leads with hormones and metabolism because that’s where the condition actually lives. Accurate language is the first step toward accurate care.

Swipe through for the full breakdown on this change.

lumeria.skin
People thought we were crazy for dropping everything to build a skincare device. Here's why we did it anyway.

Maryanne was shadowing dermatologists when she noticed the gap: clinics have the imaging tools to actually understand skin, but the moment you go home, you're back to guessing. She'd already built a 7-time award-winning biotech device by 18, and couldn't stop thinking about bringing that same imaging into people's homes.

Anthea was living that gap firsthand. Sophomore year at Berkeley, a wound that wouldn't heal: 2 months to see a doctor, 5 months to see a dermatologist, misdiagnosed 4 times, and no data to explain why nothing was working. She'd spent years in computational biology, building pipelines at Google and Boehringer Ingelheim, and knew exactly what was missing: the data to actually make sense of what her skin was doing.

One had the vision. The other had the gears turning to build the answer. Together, that became Lumeria: a multispectral device that clips onto your phone and tracks your skin the way your watch tracks your heart.

Preorders are open now. This is the start of skincare finally having real data behind it. 🌟

Both based in London. Quick context: Prism is an AI-native recruiting agency. We built our own software (best people-search tool out there - see paper in comments!) so the AI handles the grind and our recruiters focus on what actually moves the needle: client conversations, candidate calls and closes. We've placed into hedge funds and secured candidate offers at some of today's fastest growing startups. Our book is growing fast across tech, finance, and generalist roles. The two seats: Founding Recruiter - 5+ years, agency DNA. Own our biggest contracts, run the trickiest roles end-to-end, help set the playbook the team learns from. £50-80k base + 10-20% commission + 0.5-1% equity. Junior Recruiter - 0-3 years, hungry and coachable. Learn agency recruiting at speed with serious AI leverage from day one. £30-45k base + commission. Hybrid in London. Open to remote for the right person. YC asked us these questions during our interview.

1. “So... what are you working on?” (the only easy one)
2. “Why does this need to be a company? Couldn’t it just be a feature?”
3. “Isn’t this a chicken-and-egg problem? How do you get around that?”
4. “So you’re just a middleman taking a cut?”
5. “How many customers have you actually signed?”
6. “Why would customers even need to talk to you? Couldn’t they just skip you entirely?”
7. “Wouldn’t Stripe just build this? Why haven’t they already?” (we were working on agentic payments at this time)
8. “That’s a tiny market. How do you get to the big one?”
9. “Won’t everyone just use the incumbent? Everyone already uses the incumbent.”
10. “Is there any niche you could actually win first?”
11. “You said you handle [X]. How do you actually handle [X]?”
12. “You’re still in school with two years left. Why now? Why not after you graduate?”

Got this email this morning AstroCat just got featured again in 40 countries around the world. Spain, Germany, France, UK, Poland, Russia, and so many more.
Me and my dad built this from scratch. He made the entire engine. I taught myself 3D modeling, animation, and UI/UX to bring the whole world to life.
Two years ago I left a corporate job with no idea if this would work. Getting featured once felt like a miracle getting featured again, in this many countries, still doesn’t feel real.
Right now I’m deep in building the next update a whole new world, new skins, new levels. This feature couldn’t have come at a better time.
Thank you to everyone who’s followed this journey 🌍✨

evidence.title: Today we officially launch! GutGutGoose makes personalized probiotics that engineer the human microbiome. Personalization is the future of healthcare, yet the entire probiotics industry is still operating under a one-size-fits-all premise. The formulations are made without knowing anything about the individual consuming them. Everyone gets the same bacterial strains, the same dosage, and when nothing works, the customer is left to make another guess. We’ve eliminated the guessing by customizing the pill to every single person. Customers send in a stool sample, giving our testing facilities over 5GB of extensive microbiome data. An algorithm uses that data to create a digitized clone of the microbiome, test thousands of bacterial strains against it, and find ones that will colonize and be of benefit. These strains are then compiled into a supply of probiotics. Every 3 months, we test again to see how the microbiome has changed, and use the results to improve the next formula. The longitudinal gut data collected will be used in the future to be able to identify chronic diseases such as Alzheimer’s and dementia, years before they begin to affect the individual. Sign up here: https://gutgutgoose.com (link in bio) 💚🪿

Either way, the weaponization of regulatory uncertainty as a competitive tool should be completely unacceptable.

He argues there’s no need to ban Chinese open-source models — just direct agencies to issue soft-law warnings that create enough FUD so regulated enterprises back off. “It needn’t be that well justified.”

Wrong. Regulatory decisions should always be well justified and grounded in facts, logic, and evidence, not the deliberate exploitation of fear and uncertainty. Implementing a surreptitious policy through manufactured doubt — rather than strong and explicit justification — corrodes the rule of law and invites future abuse against anyone.

We are at a critical inflection point in AI policy. The leading closed labs, already a duopoly in terms of AI model revenue, want the government to eliminate their open source competition. They have laid their cards on the table. {"id":"2079599953283019166","author":"julianfried","name":"Julian Fried","text":"Love to see it","likes":18,"retweets":1,"replies":1,"views":2277,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Tue Jul 21 16:10:40 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/julianfried/status/2079599953283019166","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2079514861583642864","author":"jimfarley98","name":"Jim Farley","text":"Today, @Ford announced we’re joining forces with our founding partners at @BlackRock, @Google, and @Carhartt to form a new organization, the Alliance for America’s Skilled Trades. 

Skilled trades are at the heart of what we call the Essential Economy, the 95 million Americans who build, move, and fix the things our country depends on every day. These vital trades and industries are the backbone of the American economy, but millions of these jobs are expected to go unfilled in the years ahead. 

At Ford, we recognize the skilled trades workforce shortage is a national crisis but also a generational opportunity. Why this alliance? Well, like any big, thorny problem, no one person or organization is going to solve the skilled trades shortage alone. And so when I started talking to Larry Fink, Bayo Ogunlesi, Ruth Porat, and Linda Hubbard about these issues, we knew that we could do more together. 

We’ve got three main goals: build a jobs pipeline for skilled trades, highlight what's working across the country including the launch of a Skilled Trades Report, and grow this movement with more partners.

This is just the start. We look forward to welcoming others on board who are equally passionate about solving this for America.

Read our op-ed today in @FortuneMagazine to learn more about our collective work: https://t.co/wPZcl4jpQI

evidence.title: Your ovaries grow follicles in waves. Usually, only one from the final wave ovulates. But sometimes two follicles from the same wave both make it, releasing eggs within about 24 hours of each other during a single LH surge. That’s how fraternal twins happen. But what happens when different waves each trigger their own LH surge, days apart? First, let’s define true ovulation: it is when a follicle ruptures and releases a viable egg ready for fertilization. As we explore in this post, your biology doesn't always follow the textbook. While a standard textbook cycle has one LH surge, it's actually very common to see multiple surges on your hormone chart. For the average person, a second LH surge usually just indicates that your body attempted to ovulate, paused, and is trying again. However, biology is complex. Sometimes that second wave does cause a secondary follicle to rupture days later, hence we put “ovulate” in quotes! While a rupture happens, the hormonal environment usually prevents it from releasing a truly viable second egg. In the astronomically rare edge-cases where both events do produce a viable egg and both get fertilized (aided by the fact that sperm can survive up to 5 days), it results in superfecundation. The big takeaway is that the female body is incredibly complex, and standard diagrams oversimplify things. Swipe through to see what these different hormone signatures might look like. Your ovaries grow follicles in waves. Usually, only one from the final wave ovulates. But sometimes two follicles from the same wave both make it, releasing eggs within about 24 hours of each other during a single LH surge. That’s how fraternal twins happen.

But what happens when different waves each trigger their own LH surge, days apart?

First, let’s define true ovulation: it is when a follicle ruptures and releases a viable egg ready for fertilization.

As we explore in this post, your biology doesn't always follow the textbook. While a standard textbook cycle has one LH surge, it's actually very common to see multiple surges on your hormone chart. For the average person, a second LH surge usually just indicates that your body attempted to ovulate, paused, and is trying again.

However, biology is complex. Sometimes that second wave does cause a secondary follicle to rupture days later, hence we put “ovulate” in quotes! While a rupture happens, the hormonal environment usually prevents it from releasing a truly viable second egg.

In the astronomically rare edge-cases where both events do produce a viable egg and both get fertilized (aided by the fact that sperm can survive up to 5 days), it results in superfecundation.

The big takeaway is that the female body is incredibly complex, and standard diagrams oversimplify things.

Swipe through to see what these different hormone signatures might look like.

evidence.text: We beat Mythos and Fable 5 in <36 hours. There's been endless hype around Mythos' capabilities since its announcement, so much so that Anthropic won't release it directly and instead publicized Fable 5, a safety-capped version of the same model. So once Fable 5 was out, we @sentra_app knew we had to test just how wide the gap was between it and what was already available. We took GPT-5.5, the current leading model on Terminal-Bench 2.1, and changed one thing: we gave it Sentra's Code Memory. The result: - A score of 88.31%, ahead of Fable 5 (80.5%) and Mythos 5 (88.0%). - 3.65x cheaper than the same model without Sentra. Accuracy up, cost down ~72.6%, tokens down 41.2%. All from one change: a task-scoped memory layer that keeps the agent from re-reading context it already has. We're now submitting through Terminal-Bench's official verification and will release every agent trajectory once

evidence.text: you’re asking the right question. measurement without a closed loop is just another dashboard. that’s where every quantified-self device dies. evidence.text: We're excited to introduce Archal publicly, the first deterministic eval platform for AI agents. {"id":"2064431203126829352","author":"agentphonehq","name":"AgentPhone (YC P26)","text":"we're going to make this huge","likes":14,"retweets":1,"replies":1,"views":1403,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Tue Jun 09 19:35:28 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/agentphonehq/status/2064431203126829352","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2064422792691692017","author":"jamesfong","name":"James Fong","text":"📱 @AgentPhoneHQ gives every AI agent its own phone number, so an agent can actually call, text, and authenticate in the real world. They handle all the telecom compliance behind the scenes, so the agent just signs up over an API and starts making calls and sending messages.

The whole telecom stack was built for humans, which is why agents hit a wall the moment they need to do something as basic as receive a verification code or make a call. Manav and Meet spent months becoming official CPAAS vendors and getting compliant before they ever launched, which is the kind of unglamorous groundwork that turns into a real moat. It's working. Agents are already signing up on their own through the API, and AgentPhone is the default phone number option on Google's Agent Dev Kit, Vercel, Replit, and Langchain. As more agents come online, that distribution compounds.

https://t.co/323VyupN7b

What makes me even more excited is who's building it. @manav2modi and @themeetmodi are brothers who have been building together their whole lives. @pioneer_fund is excited to back them as they give agents a way to reach the rest of us. Congrats!

evidence.title: We’re proud to announce our $5M pre-seed round led by Andreessen Horowitz Real estate investing is still stuck in the past. Spreadsheets, PDFs, months-long transactions, and decisions made on incomplete information. The technology exists to change this, but the infrastructure doesn’t. We’re building the AI operating system that changes that. A platform that ingests live data, underwrites properties automatically, and executes deals in real time. What used to take six months now happens in minutes, and institutional-grade intelligence becomes accessible to everyone. This round was led by Andreessen Horowitz, with backing from Harvard Business School, Techstars, 500 Global, Cornerstone VC, South Loop Ventures, Cento Ventures, Anker Capital, and Tomahawk.VC. We’re also supported by angels from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind, Airbnb, and Blackstone. We started in Dubai, but today we’re already building for global markets, including London, New York, Miami, Riyadh, and beyond. This was never meant to be a local proptech story. It’s global infrastructure. This is just the beginning!

Real estate investing is still stuck in the past. Spreadsheets, PDFs, months-long transactions, and decisions made on incomplete information. The technology exists to change this, but the infrastructure doesn’t.

We’re building the AI operating system that changes that. A platform that ingests live data, underwrites properties automatically, and executes deals in real time. What used to take six months now happens in minutes, and institutional-grade intelligence becomes accessible to everyone.

We started in Dubai, but today we’re already building for global markets, including London, New York, Miami, Riyadh, and beyond. This was never meant to be a local proptech story. It’s global infrastructure.

This is just the beginning!

evidence.text: If you want to own your models and data, reach out to us!
evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2082556717376909735","author":"hiloopai","name":"hiloop (YC S26)","text":"If you want to own your models and data, reach out to us!","likes":6,"retweets":4,"replies":0,"views":1034,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Wed Jul 29 19:59:48 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/hiloopai/status/2082556717376909735","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2082556286340874383","author":"deepmatmul","name":"Karan Brar","text":"Every AI company should own its data, its models, and the research lab that keeps making them better.

Today, @tboser and I are launching @hiloopai to make that possible.

The frontier advantage isn’t access to a model. It’s the research organization continuously improving it.

Your product already generates the raw material for better intelligence: proprietary data, production feedback, evaluations, and domain expertise. Very few teams have the research capacity to turn those assets into better models.

Hiloop builds and operates that capability with you.

Bring us the model your product depends on, the data that makes it different, and an evaluation that defines success. We reproduce your baseline and run an autonomous research campaign against it.

Agents pursue competing hypotheses in parallel, build on previous results, and promote only improvements that survive verification. Our researchers validate the winners and bring them into production.

The work can run hosted or inside your environment. You retain control of your data, and the resulting models, evaluations, and research artifacts are yours.

We’re starting with model training, post-training, and inference optimization, where progress is measurable and the value is immediate.

But this isn’t a one-off model improvement. It’s a persistent research capability that begins each campaign with everything learned from the last.

Over time, the lab accumulates research memory and improves its own tools, evaluations, and agents. The process used to create better intelligence gets better itself.

That’s infrastructure for recursive self-improvement.

If your product depends on a model and an important metric has stopped moving, bring us the model you can’t make better. We're much better at research than making videos!

Reach out to us: founders@hiloop.ai","created_at":"Wed Jul 29 19:58:05 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/deepmatmul/status/2082556286340874383","has_media":true,"media_urls":["https://video.twimg.com/amplify_video/2082555861755674624/vid/avc1/480x270/gUiLXbuIGiAEthme.mp4?tag=29"],"media_posters":["https://pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb/2082555861755674624/img/ypYqYJ2ebfsxxbuo.jpg"]}}

{"profile":null,"gridUrl":{"caption":"Player 🎮 > Creator 😎 > Dev 🤓

@kairostime_gaming is officially a Game Dev at Antihero Studios! 

We’re putting the FUN back in mobile games and cutting the bs.

Who’s ready for games you actually want to share with friends? 

🎮 WHAT IS MISFITZ?

Misfitz is a top-down mobile extraction shooter where the fast-paced combat of Brawl Stars meets the high-stakes tension of ARC Raiders.

In a world “over-optimized” by Zero, you play as a Misfitz—a neon-stainted rebel breaking into machine-run streets to steal back human culture locked away as Relics.

{"id":"2024306494620258597","author":"segalbenji","name":"Ben Segal","text":"Big news - @Variant_ai_dtc is now backed by @speedrun , @a16z's early-stage fund! 

Variant’s team is locked the F in on solving one of the biggest problems for brands - delivering the right content, to the right people, at the right time. 

Brands are drowning in data but starving for action.

Customer signals are scattered across platforms, but turning that into coordinated execution still requires weeks of planning across data, design, engineering and growth teams.

Variant turns that mess into continuous execution:
- Unifying signals, analyzing behavior and understanding intent.
- Decides what each person should see.
- Build, deploy and test experiences automatically.

The website is phase one. The rest of the journey is next.

The pace and momentum are wild:

We’re onboarding new brands daily, helping them create real incremental revenue. Referrals are compounding. 
Some of which are world-class brands I could only imagine working with a few months back.

evidence.title: Let’s talk about poop for a second. 💩 I say this all the time: gut health isn’t just about how often you go — it’s about what’s actually happening in there. Diversity of your microbiome matters. And in this modern world of processed food, stress, and antibiotics, dysbiosis (an imbalanced gut) is driving way more inflammation than most people realize. Here’s the problem with most probiotics: they’re generic. Same strains, same dose, for every single person — regardless of what your gut actually needs. And research shows up to 77% of those generic strains don’t even colonize. You’re probably taking a fraction of the dose your gut actually needs to make a difference. That’s why I’m interested in @gutgutgoose - Instead of guessing, they sequence your microbiome from an at-home stool test, model how different probiotic strains would actually perform in your gut specifically, and compound a formula built around your results. Then you retest and adjust — so it evolves with you instead of staying static. Looks-maxxing your dog this summer

We rounded up the grooming + skincare we actually reach for.

→ liv luv dog wipes — the daily, compostable, low-effort clean
→ redecker dog brush — the quiet-money pick. Handmade in germany since 1935
→ Biche cloud cleanser — pH-balanced, sulfate- and paraben-free, built with a vet derm
→ Masco beauty aloha dog spf30 — the summer non-negotiable (sun damage is cumulative, even on dogs)
→ Hermès dog brush — the splurge. Beechwood, steel pins, grooming-as-ritual energy

Here’s the thing though: the glow is downstream of the health. a shiny coat, clear skin, good energy — that’s what’s actually happening underneath, made visible. Products help your dog look well. Knowing what’s going on under the surface is how you keep them being well. That’s the part we’re building.

—
not sponsored. no affiliate links, no freebies, no codes. just things we genuinely love for our own pets. always patch-test new products and check with your vet before introducing anything new, especially for dogs with sensitive skin or known allergies.

evidence.text: Big news for Cosmic Robotics on joining the Y Combinator Summer batch. Cosmic Robotics builds autonomous construction equipment to build critical infrastructure. Starting here on Earth and eventually to build a city on Mars. I’m proud to share the work Hello Robo did for them — we had the privilege of designing Constellation, their digital twin and robot management software platform, built to give operators a clear, confident view into their fleet. It’s so much easier and smoother to work with founders who care about UX and Design. Thanks to James Emerick and Lewis C Jones for being creative partners, not clients. Proud of what we built together, and excited to see where Cosmic Robotics goes from here. …more
evidence.rawVisibleText: Feed post number 4 James Emerick James Emerick • 3rd+ Premium • 3rd+ Accelerating the construction of critical infrastructure. Accelerating the construction of critical infrastructure. 2d • 2 days ago • Visible to anyone on or off LinkedIn Follow Good design is under appreciated in robotics. {"id":"2064431088064483777","author":"manav2modi","name":"Manav Modi","text":"Super excited to be backed by @pioneer_fund!!","likes":4,"retweets":0,"replies":3,"views":510,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Tue Jun 09 19:35:01 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/manav2modi/status/2064431088064483777","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2064422792691692017","author":"jamesfong","name":"James Fong","text":"📱 @AgentPhoneHQ gives every AI agent its own phone number, so an agent can actually call, text, and authenticate in the real world. They handle all the telecom compliance behind the scenes, so the agent just signs up over an API and starts making calls and sending messages.

The whole telecom stack was built for humans, which is why agents hit a wall the moment they need to do something as basic as receive a verification code or make a call. Manav and Meet spent months becoming official CPAAS vendors and getting compliant before they ever launched, which is the kind of unglamorous groundwork that turns into a real moat. It's working. Agents are already signing up on their own through the API, and AgentPhone is the default phone number option on Google's Agent Dev Kit, Vercel, Replit, and Langchain. As more agents come online, that distribution compounds.

https://t.co/323VyupN7b

What makes me even more excited is who's building it. @manav2modi and @themeetmodi are brothers who have been building together their whole lives. @pioneer_fund is excited to back them as they give agents a way to reach the rest of us. Congrats!

She puts the strap on the way she always does, one hand steadying it while the other reaches for something on the ledge. It takes a few seconds, no different from checking a watch.

The dog is already close, ears up, because he knows what's coming. She crouches low, under the laundry line still hung with yesterday's wash, a small piece of food held between two fingers.

She doesn't just hand it over. She waits half a second, judging when his mouth is actually ready, then lets go. He takes it too eagerly, the way he always does, and she laughs under her breath, not really meant for anyone.

Nothing here was staged. It's a courtyard, a dog, a Tuesday like most others: buckets doing double duty as planters, tiled floor worn smooth in patches, a gate left open to the street. For a few minutes, a small camera on her head is quietly recording exactly how she does it, the crouch, the half-second wait, the precise release nobody taught her, she just knows.

Somewhere far from this courtyard, that ordinary rhythm is becoming something else.

Human to Machine Symbiosis.

evidence.title: Artin Bogdanov built his first company to $8 million in revenue by 22. Bootstrapped, no VC, 50 suppliers, 300% year-over-year growth. Then Google changed one advertising policy and his entire distribution disappeared overnight. He sued Google. The company didn’t survive. The automation tools he built for that first company became the foundation of his second startup, which grew to 20,000 e-commerce customers. When Canva came to acquire it, the deal collapsed because his team was in Moscow and Russia had just invaded Ukraine. He walked away again. Now he’s building Sun, an AI app that generates personalized audio content on demand, backed by a16z through Speedrun (0.3% acceptance rate). He describes his three companies as three motivations: applying raw energy, trying to be financially smart, and what he calls a “child of love.” What’s one failure that taught you exactly what to build next? Drop it below. Follow for more on the inner game of building and scaling businesses. evidence.title: We're hiring another Customer Success Manager at Dayjob to support our growing customer base.
evidence.text:
We're hiring another Customer Success Manager at Dayjob to support our growing customer base.

We build AI agents for waste trucks, one of the largest, least-digitised sectors of the economy. 

This year we got backed by Y Combinator, are live with 13 paying customers, and are growing fast.

Our customers run real fleets, with real operational complexity. A 5% improvement in routing efficiency is worth hundreds of thousands of pounds a year to them. We take that seriously. 

We want every customer to feel the impact of what we're building, and this role is central to making that happen.

This is a field-first role: three days a week at customer depots across the UK, the rest at our Camden office. You'll own a portfolio of accounts end-to-end, drive measurable efficiency gains, and help build the CS function from the ground up.

The kind of person who will love this:

- Gets energy from being on-site and around straight-talking people 
- Wants to build something from scratch
- Takes full ownership and doesn't wait to be told

£50k to £90k depending on level of experience, plus equity.

Full details in the spec in comments. If someone in your network would be a great fit, tag them or send it their way.

{"id":"2035823831965999579","author":"gustrigos","name":"Gus Trigos","text":"This is a big part of why we started Runtime.","likes":3,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":592,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Sun Mar 22 20:59:59 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/gustrigos/status/2035823831965999579","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2035773341873963091","author":"larsencc","name":"Larsen Cundric","text":"At @browser_use we run millions of parallel agents. We think about parallelism all day. That's the job.

It got me thinking about something most teams aren't talking about yet.

Picture a 50 person engineering org where everyone uses AI coding assistants. Each developer kicks off a few agents at once. Suddenly you have hundreds of concurrent code changes being generated, tested, and pushed.

Now ask yourself: where does all that code get validated?

For most companies, the answer is a single staging environment. Maybe two if they're lucky.

That's a massive mismatch. Your development throughput just 10x'd, but your validation layer stayed exactly the same. Agents sit idle waiting their turn. Context windows expire. CI pipelines pile up. The productivity gains you paid for evaporate in a queue.

This isn't an agent problem. It's an infrastructure problem. Staging was built for a world where one person ships one thing, gets feedback, iterates. That model breaks when the workload becomes parallel by default.

I've seen this pattern before, even pre-AI. At Flexport, the product was so large you couldn't run it locally. Every engineer got their own cloud dev environment. Docker containers spun up on demand, with switches to toggle which services you needed. Not because it was fancy. Because one shared environment for hundreds of engineers simply didn't work.

Now give each of those engineers 3 agents (or more ofc).

Teams keep throwing money at better models and faster agents while ignoring the chokepoint sitting right behind them. You invested in 10x development speed and got 2x back because the rest is stuck waiting.

The answer is ephemeral, isolated environments. One per agent. Spun up in seconds, torn down when done. Only the services that changed get deployed. No shared state, no queue, no conflicts.

Every serious engineering org will need this. Most haven't even started thinking about it.

So who's building this? Because most teams are holding together shared environments with duct tape and hoping it scales.

If you're working on this or running into it, I want to hear from you.","created_at":"Sun Mar 22 17:39:22 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/larsencc/status/2035773341873963091","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

evidence.title: We couldn't get runtime .com.
evidence.text: We couldn't get runtime .com. So for the first month, we were runtm. Our first product was an open source CLI that let coding agents deploy to production. runtm, all lowercase. Looked clean for dev tools. But people started calling us Run TM. RunTM. Meanwhile the product outgrew the CLI. PMs, designers, marketers started showing up alongside the devs. We needed a real brand. So we went back to what we meant all along: Runtime. In software, runtime is the final phase of the dev lifecycle. When code stops living on your machine and starts being useful to the world. That's exactly the gap we close. runtm .com is five characters, easy to remember, and already pulling 10k+ unique visits a week. Guess what we paid for it 🤑

The longevity industry is coming for your dog. Most of what it’s about to sell you is a waste of money — and some of it has never been tested for safety in dogs at all.

Here’s what actually moves the needle, and none of it comes in a vial.

In one 14-year study, Labrador littermates fed 25% fewer calories lived 1.8 years longer. Nothing on the supplement market comes close to that.

The real protocol is unglamorous: notice things earlier than your dog needs you to, feed a little less than you think they need, move them more than is convenient, keep their mind working, and read the pattern instead of reacting to one bad moment.

Because the question was never “how old is my dog.” It’s “how is my dog aging” — and the only way to answer that is to watch the trend over time, not stare at a single number.

Article in collaboration with vet student @niharika_edke.
Link in bio 🔗

evidence.title: Early-stage founders face an impossible trade-off: You need data-driven decisions to grow. But building proper models takes time and expertise you don't have. And hiring someone to do it? You can't afford that yet. So you're stuck making gut calls... or worse, no calls at all. For years, sophisticated financial planning was a luxury reserved for Fortune 1000 companies with 100-person finance teams. But that's changing. The power of data-driven decision-making is moving downmarket. Mid-market companies and startups can now access tools that let them model scenarios, run forecasts, and make strategic decisions at the same speed as enterprise, without the enterprise overhead. And here's why that matters: Speed is an edge. If you can make better decisions faster than your competitors, you're more likely to win. The companies that figure out how to move fast with confidence (not just fast with guesswork) will have a massive advantage. For the first time, you don't need an army of analysts to operate like you do.

Early-stage founders face an impossible trade-off:

You need data-driven decisions to grow. But building proper models takes time and expertise you don't have. And hiring someone to do it? You can't afford that yet.

So you're stuck making gut calls... or worse, no calls at all.

For years, sophisticated financial planning was a luxury reserved for Fortune 1000 companies with 100-person finance teams.

But that's changing.

The power of data-driven decision-making is moving downmarket.

Mid-market companies and startups can now access tools that let them model scenarios, run forecasts, and make strategic decisions at the same speed as enterprise, without the enterprise overhead.

And here's why that matters:

Speed is an edge. If you can make better decisions faster than your competitors, you're more likely to win.

The companies that figure out how to move fast with confidence (not just fast with guesswork) will have a massive advantage.

For the first time, you don't need an army of analysts to operate like you do.

每個家長都想畀小朋友最好的教育，但最矛盾的是，我們往往用最多的時間去換取資源，卻失去了陪伴他們成長的最珍貴時刻。

evidence.title: We tested SUN against NotebookLM and Spotify's AI podcast workflow in a 600-match blind benchmark, and SUN came out on top. Read benchmark: sunapp.ai/blog What if AI-generated podcasts could be measured the same way we measure chess players? We set out to answer a simple question: which AI system creates the most engaging educational audio? We ran a blind benchmark comparing SUN Course, SUN Podcast, NotebookLM, and Save-to-Spotify across 100 topics and multiple episode lengths. The judges were GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, evaluating 600 head-to-head comparisons without knowing which system created each script. The results were clear. SUN Course ranked #1 with an Elo score of 1160, followed by SUN Podcast at 1118, NotebookLM at 963, and Save-to-Spotify at 758. In direct matchups, SUN Course won 191 out of 300 comparisons, and at 30-minute duration achieved an 88% win rate. The benchmark focused on listenability, structure, engagement, and educational value, measuring content quality rather than voice synthesis. The takeaway: SUN generated the most engaging long-form educational audio among the systems tested.

We tested SUN against NotebookLM and Spotify's AI podcast workflow in a 600-match blind benchmark, and SUN came out on top.

Read benchmark:
sunapp.ai/blog

What if AI-generated podcasts could be measured the same way we measure chess players?

We set out to answer a simple question: which AI system creates the most engaging educational audio?

We ran a blind benchmark comparing SUN Course, SUN Podcast, NotebookLM, and Save-to-Spotify across 100 topics and multiple episode lengths. The judges were GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, and Gemini 3.1 Pro, evaluating 600 head-to-head comparisons without knowing which system created each script.

The results were clear. SUN Course ranked #1 with an Elo score of 1160, followed by SUN Podcast at 1118, NotebookLM at 963, and Save-to-Spotify at 758.

In direct matchups, SUN Course won 191 out of 300 comparisons, and at 30-minute duration achieved an 88% win rate.

The benchmark focused on listenability, structure, engagement, and educational value, measuring content quality rather than voice synthesis.

The takeaway: SUN generated the most engaging long-form educational audio among the systems tested.

Today, we announced a $5M Seed round to build the next generation of AI-native analysis for finance.

The round includes participation from @speedrun , @getdeel, The Perseverance Fund, StandUp Ventures, @altaircapital, and a group of strategic angels.

Modern finance teams don’t have a data problem.

They have an analysis problem.

While systems of record and dashboards have improved dramatically over the past decade, the leap from data to decisions remains slow and manual.

Pluvo is building an AI-native, agentic analysis engine designed to operate in that gap; transforming data into structured insights, and insights into faster, higher-quality decisions.

Today, Pluvo partners with forward-thinking teams at companies including @nookshq , and @ninety.io, supporting growth-stage and mid-market finance leaders as they modernize their planning and analysis workflows.
This new capital will accelerate product development, expand Pluvo’s agentic capabilities, and deepen its decision intelligence platform.

We’re grateful to our investors, customers, and team for their continued belief in the mission.

Boards aren't just asking about AI anymore. They're pushing for it across the entire business.

And honestly? That's putting CFOs in a new position.

It's not just about finance efficiency. It's about looking at every department and asking: where are we still doing manual, repetitive work that AI could handle?

Because here's what we're seeing in our conversations with finance leaders:

When you automate the tedious stuff, teams get to focus on the strategic work that actually moves the business forward.

Better margins. Better efficiency. Higher valuation.

The companies that embed AI across their operations (not just in one department) are the ones that become more attractive and set up for long-term success.

If you're still treating AI as a finance-only initiative, you're missing the bigger opportunity.

There is one part of building a startup I never get tired of.

Not fundraising.
Not decks.
Not metrics.

Prototyping concepts!

Building a startup is stressful, exhausting, and demanding.

Designing prototype concepts is the rare part that still feels like play.

It is where ideas stop being opinions and start to feel real.

Prototypes are about questions.

What does an audio-first product look like without visual noise?
What happens when an interface respects attention instead of fighting for it?
What emotions do we want users to feel while learning?
How minimal can learning feel without becoming empty?

These screens are experiments, not answers.

Prototyping lets us think with our hands.
It is the fastest way to turn philosophy into product.

This is where SUN takes form.

Comment “SUN” if you want early access to SUN 🙂

evidence.title: one of the best advices I got talking to @AnthropicAI team was to "let @claude think".
evidence.text: one of the best advices I got talking to @AnthropicAI team was to "let @claude think". as @trq212 wrote here, it made a huge difference to go from prescriptive imperatives (e.g. change this fn to do this) -> explaining the outcome and letting it reason through (e.g. I want X what are we missing in the current implementation). is the level of anthropomorphizing here spooky? yes its as if the models are growing up/mirroring some level of human development; as the models get larger and the reasoning capabilities more complex, the human/model interface is also getting more abstract.

“The idea that women’s bodies are predictable and interchangeable is one of the biggest myths in healthcare.” - @jennysduan in an exclusive interview with @the_newsette⁠
⁠
For decades, women have been expected to navigate their health with limited research, limited data, and a lot of guesswork.⁠ 🤷‍♀️⁠
⁠
Now, @clair_health has raised $11.6 million to build a wearable designed specifically for women’s hormones, aiming to give women more insight into what’s happening inside their bodies.⁠
⁠
It's clear that women’s health has long been underfunded despite representing half the population. That’s beginning to change, and it’s opening the door for more founders to build solutions for fertility, menopause, hormonal health, and beyond. 👏

Subscribe to @the_newsette for free at the link in bio.

There's a version of your skin story that a regular photo just can't tell.

Normal light only shows what's on the surface. The signals that tell you whether your routine is working, often weeks before you'd notice with your eyes alone.

It's the difference between "I think this serum is working" and "I know this serum is working."

That gap is exactly what we built Lumeria to close.

evidence.title: No kid meltdowns?!
evidence.text: No kid meltdowns?! Is this a utopia?
evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2082468986311311497","author":"themichelinmin","name":"Min","text":"No kid meltdowns?! Is this a utopia?","likes":1,"retweets":0,"replies":1,"views":245,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Wed Jul 29 14:11:11 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/themichelinmin/status/2082468986311311497","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2082429475921293324","author":"robbiehendricks","name":"Robbie Hendricks","text":"Couple societal takeaways from Lake Como that stuck out:

1) No one wore smart watches except Americans. European tourists and locals wore either no watch at all or analog.

2) Tons of kids, no tablets. I didn’t see one tablet the entire trip until I got to the airport. No kids on phones. 

3) Kids were at dinner with parents and were engaged. And parents engaged with kids. Sometimes kids played cards or colored, but more often they were just present. Saw a phone come out ONE time for a toddler.

4) I barely saw any packaged food like chips or cookies. This may be unique to a vacation destinations like Como, but I didn’t see any kids or families with packaged food. Tons of fruit. Even as we walked through town, saw nothing…not even for sale.

5) Kids at dinner ate what their parents ate - meat, vegetables, bread. No whining, no bending over backwards to find things a kid will eat. 

6) Mentioned this to my wife the final day - we didn’t see one child cry or have a tantrum. Kids ranged from 3-8 all over this place, and I didn’t see one meltdown. I realize this is anecdotal, but it really stuck out.

I’ll acknowledge this was a beautiful hotel in a high end area, so the standards of these folks may be different than your average person.

That said, the parenting style, connections with kids, and food really stuck out. I’m around wealthy folks in America and it’s wildly different.

And the watches. 

I can confidently say I didn’t see one Apple Watch or Garmin the entire time I was in Italy. It is obvious the (over) optimization culture is uniquely American.

(I had time to write this post because our flight was cancelled, of course)","created_at":"Wed Jul 29 11:34:11 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/robbiehendricks/status/2082429475921293324","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

evidence.text: Being a founder = being so good at getting rejected/ghosted its not cute ✨ but you keep asking anyways
evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2050290184210501792","author":"jihprobs","name":"jihyun","text":"Being a founder = being so good at getting rejected/ghosted its not cute ✨ but you keep asking anyways","likes":4,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":288,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Fri May 01 19:04:07 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/jihprobs/status/2050290184210501792","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2049946550915506351","author":"Clara_Gold","name":"Clara Gold","text":"I realized fundraising was the first time in my life I got rejected at scale. And honestly, as a woman, I was not emotionally trained for it.

Before the feminists come for me, let me make my point.

I think the first real arena where most people experience power, desire, status, and rejection is dating.

And dating trains men brutally. 

A lot of men learn very early that if they want someone, they have to walk across the room, risk looking stupid, get rejected, survive it, and do it again. They learn that rejection is volume, timing, targeting. It’s a numbers game.

A lot of women are trained very differently. 

Especially if you’re a pretty girl, you don’t usually walk into a bar looking at a guy thinking: “Can I have him?” You only think: “Do I want him?”. 

You don’t build your identity around shooting your shot 100 times and surviving 99 no’s. You don’t get trained to ask directly, get rejected publicly, and act normal 5 minutes later. 

You get trained to be “chosen”. To be impressive enough that the opportunity comes to you.

And then you start building a company. 

And the whole paradigm changes. Suddenly, everyone can say no to you. Investors say no. Candidates say no. Customers say no.

And when your rejection muscle is weak, your brain does the dumbest thing possible: it makes the “no” mean something about you. That you’re not smart enough. Not compelling enough.

I think this is one of the most underrated gender differences in fundraising. 

Not that men are inherently better at it. But a lot of them have built thicker rejection scar tissue earlier. They know how to hear no and keep moving. They know how to make it less personal. They know how to treat it like volume, timing, targeting, iteration.

I didn’t. 

I’ve raised 3 rounds. On the surface, the story looks great: I raised with Sequoia, OpenAI, Khosla. Woohoo.

The real story is less sexy: every round wrecked me. I lost 5kg each time. I probably donated a few years of life expectancy to the cap table.

Because every round, I only got 1 term sheet. One. EVERYONE else said no. And when almost everyone says no, your body does not care about the intellectually correct explanation. It only hears: Maybe they’re right. Maybe you’re not that compelling. Maybe you’re not the founder you thought you were.

For a long time, I thought confidence meant learning not to take the no personally. I don’t believe that anymore. Maybe some people are built like that. I’m not.

30 years of being trained to be chosen does not turn into resilience because someone in a Patagonia vest says fundraising is a numbers game.

So now I think confidence is something less glamorous. 

Confidence is taking the no very personally. Letting it ruin your day, losing your appetite, spiraling for hours… And still taking the next meeting.

Confidence is just being bothered as f*** and not letting it make you smaller.

I still don’t fully believe my own BS as I’m writing this, but I guess that’s the point. Can’t wait for the next round to find out.","created_at":"Thu Apr 30 20:18:38 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/Clara_Gold/status/2049946550915506351","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

6 things for your pet that are actually worth your money:

1. A balanced diet (not just kibble) to provide proper nutrients and health long term along with vitamins.

2. Toys that stimulate your dog’s brain - super important for cognitive function.

3. Omi Health’s AI chat answers any questions I have on my dog’s health with data backed by vets. Now I know my dog’s biological age and I was able to test over 40 of her biomarkers which has been life changing for her health.

4. Sniffing on walks - tires them out faster than physical exercise and reduces stress.

5. Bone broth - helps joint health, soothes stomach and gives extra hydration.

6. Portable water bottle - great for when you’re on the go especially in the summer.

For years, people have talked about connecting strategy to finance. Making CFOs truly strategic. Unlocking the potential of financial data.

But the way companies approached it was limited by technology.

People built faster spreadsheets, bigger databases, and more integrations.

And still, the analysis landed on the individual. Once you had all this data, it was your job to make sense of it.

The technology has finally caught up.

We can now operationalize and embed a lot of that analysis. We're on the front end of a new wave: embedded autonomous analysis for enterprise.

This is what gets us excited about what we're building at Pluvo.

Finance is shifting from being isolated to being embedded across the whole business. Tools like Campfire and Rillet are building AI-powered ERPs that create workflows and automations faster than legacy systems ever could.

This is the perfect moment to shift planning from strictly a finance thing to a decision-making system for the whole business.

The gap between vision and capability is closing. The companies that move now will define the category.

evidence.title: I fully prescribe to this now.
evidence.text: I fully prescribe to this now. I spent over a decade selling debt as the primary product for a bank. Since becoming a business owner, I truly see how debt becomes an unnecessary part of your decision making process to making your business bigger.
evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2081403578309345449","author":"themichelinmin","name":"Min","text":"I fully prescribe to this now. I spent over a decade selling debt as the primary product for a bank. Since becoming a business owner, I truly see how debt becomes an unnecessary part of your decision making process to making your business bigger.","likes":1,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":270,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Sun Jul 26 15:37:38 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/themichelinmin/status/2081403578309345449","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2081371672192397669","author":"Budgetdog_","name":"Brennan Schlagbaum, CPA","text":"I paid off my 2.375% mortgage at 28.

People told me it was the dumbest financial decision I could make.

“You’ll regret it.”

“You’ll earn more investing.”

“That debt is basically free.”

What they missed was the entire point.

I wasn’t just paying off a mortgage.

I was buying the confidence to leave my 9-5 and bet on myself.

That decision helped me build a business that made me far more than the market ever would have on that money.

So yes, I won the psychological debate.

I also won the math debate based on the timing of the payoff working in my favor.

And for everyone who said I’d regret it…

I can take out another mortgage whenever I want.

I still haven’t.

People love optimizing returns on paper while ignoring the decisions that change their life.","created_at":"Sun Jul 26 13:30:51 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/Budgetdog_/status/2081371672192397669","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

evidence.text: Finally someone talking about this.
evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2058763541025521804","author":"kacppian","name":"Kaushik","text":"Finally someone talking about this.","likes":1,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":33,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Mon May 25 04:14:12 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/kacppian/status/2058763541025521804","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2058660802425438459","author":"adamshuaib","name":"Adam Shuaib","text":"After 15 years of investing, we realised that truly exceptional founders have something impossible to fake: deeply unconventional lives.

We analysed 15,000 founders using five binary signals to measure this: odd hobbies, early signs of exceptionalism, extreme life choices, unusual geographies, non-linear careers. These sum to give a 0-5 score per founder. Whether someone started coding at 10, speaks five languages, climbed Everest or quit a safe job to live in Chile, the signal was deviation from the mean.

Rather than focusing on IQ or EQ, we call this metric the Outlier Quotient, or “OQ”. When forecasting founder success, it turns out that OQ was the single most predictive variable in our entire classification model, trained on ~70 different factors.

Our OQ score had zero correlation with having worked at a top-tier company or attending an elite university. The signals most VCs rely on aren’t just noisy, they’re blinding. The best founders don’t signal like everyone else, they don’t think like everyone else, and they certainly don’t build like everyone else. 

If you want to spot breakout talent before the rest of the market, stop screening for conformity. Back the founders the system was built to filter out.","created_at":"Sun May 24 21:25:58 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/adamshuaib/status/2058660802425438459","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

Our hosted version took it to the next level!","likes":0,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":292,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Thu Mar 26 20:38:21 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/gustrigos/status/2037267938311553482","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2037190688950161709","author":"patrickc","name":"Patrick Collison","text":"When @karpathy built MenuGen (https://t.co/2OjrUJ3aLS), he said:

"Vibe coding menugen was exhilarating and fun escapade as a local demo, but a bit of a painful slog as a deployed, real app. Building a modern app is a bit like assembling IKEA future. There are all these services, docs, API keys, configurations, dev/prod deployments, team and security features, rate limits, pricing tiers."

We've all run into this issue when building with agents: you have to scurry off to establish accounts, clicking things in the browser as though it's the antediluvian days of 2023, in order to unblock its superintelligent progress.

So we decided to build Stripe Projects to help agents instantly provision services from the CLI.

For example, simply run:

$ stripe projects add posthog/analytics

And it'll create a PostHog account, get an API key, and (as needed) set up billing.

Projects is launching today as a developer preview. You can register for access (we'll make it available to everyone soon) at https://t.co/1tSgGbSLxM. We're also rolling out support for many new providers over the coming weeks. (Get in touch if you'd like to make your service available.)

evidence.title: Skip git worktrees.
evidence.text: Skip git worktrees. Go straight to micro-VMs. Everyone's discovering worktrees for running parallel agents. But also figuring out why they are so annoying to work with. Worktrees solve branch isolation but inherit every limitation of your local machine. Port conflicts, dependency clashes, secrets leaking between sessions. Four agents in parallel and your laptop is cooked. I spin up an ephemeral micro-VM per agent session. Dependencies pre-installed, secrets injected, own ports, own preview URL. The only set up required is snapshotting your environment once. It then rebuilds on every change to main. Every new agent session boots from that snapshot in milliseconds. This is how I'm running 20+ parallel agent sessions this way. Even Cursor and Conductor are now moving agent workflows to the cloud.

evidence.title: Let's talk about something uncomfortable... why finance leaders don't share numbers with their teams. The answer? Fear. Fear that the team will react poorly to bad financial performance. Fear that transparency will create panic. Fear that people won't understand the context. So numbers get hidden. Or they're shown in a sanitized, cookie-cutter way at quarterly all-hands meetings. High-level. Generic. Safe. But here's the thing: Poor financial performance is exactly when your team needs transparency most. Because if people don't know what's actually happening, they can't help fix it. Your sales team can't adjust their approach if they don't know pipeline conversion is down. Your marketing team can't shift strategy if they don't see that CAC is climbing. Your ops team can't find efficiencies if they don't understand the margin pressure. Hiding the numbers doesn't protect your team. It just keeps them in the dark. And when people don't have context, they fill in the blanks with speculation. Which is almost always worse than the truth. Sharing bad news is hard. But transparency doesn't mean dumping raw data on people with no context. It means showing them what's happening, why it matters, and what needs to change. Your team is capable of handling reality. What they can't handle is operating blind. Give them the information they need to help turn things around.

Fear that the team will react poorly to bad financial performance. Fear that transparency will create panic. Fear that people won't understand the context.

So numbers get hidden. Or they're shown in a sanitized, cookie-cutter way at quarterly all-hands meetings. High-level. Generic. Safe.

But here's the thing:

Poor financial performance is exactly when your team needs transparency most.

Because if people don't know what's actually happening, they can't help fix it.

Your sales team can't adjust their approach if they don't know pipeline conversion is down. Your marketing team can't shift strategy if they don't see that CAC is climbing. Your ops team can't find efficiencies if they don't understand the margin pressure.

Hiding the numbers doesn't protect your team. It just keeps them in the dark.

And when people don't have context, they fill in the blanks with speculation. Which is almost always worse than the truth.

Sharing bad news is hard. But transparency doesn't mean dumping raw data on people with no context.

It means showing them what's happening, why it matters, and what needs to change.

Your team is capable of handling reality. What they can't handle is operating blind.

Give them the information they need to help turn things around.

One of the coolest moments we’ve had building Control Seat happened last week.

A customer operated a battery in Chile from their laptop while on vacation in Hawaii. 🌎⚡

The command traveled from Hawaii to our MQTT broker in Virginia, out to the battery in Chile, and back as live telemetry.

The coolest part wasn’t the demo.

Before Control Seat, they were maintaining MQTT brokers, cloud VMs, databases, dashboards, and custom APIs just to monitor and control their batteries.

Now they do it all from one platform.

That’s exactly why we built Control Seat. We’d much rather see engineers spending their time building great products than maintaining infrastructure.

Huge thanks to Alejandro and everyone at Battex for trusting us, pushing the platform hard, and helping us make the platform better.

Read the full case study at the link in our bio.
