evidence.rawVisibleText:
{"id":"2051886366284456095","author":"perandex","name":"Stephen (Perandex)","text":"😭","likes":1,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":236,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Wed May 06 04:46:46 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/perandex/status/2051886366284456095","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2051744309641191503","author":"dfranke","name":"Daniel Franke","text":"You buy a German anvil. It contains 83 moving parts and requires winding twice a day. It's forged from excellent steel, holds tolerances across all three striking faces to within three microns, includes a beautifully indexed horn-adjustment mechanism nobody asked for, and requires a proprietary 11-point spanner should you need to replace the rebound calibration bushing. It runs flawlessly for years, but one day it starts up in limp mode because the onboard anvil-management system detects that it's overdue for its 50,000-strike inspection.

You search AliExpress for a Chinese anvil, and are presented with a multitude of offerings from such household-name brands as DUKXJYIBF, HDBTGMXI, AND UEJQIP. They're all priced to within a few pennies of each other, appear completely identical except for the nameplate, and obviously all came out of the same factory. You text your blacksmith friend to ask if they're legit. He tells you he got one like that from KIXJBU a few years ago, and that it's been great and a terrific deal. You thank him, but KIXJBU seems to have folded so you buy the one from UEJQIP. When it arrives, it feels suspiciously light. You scratch it and realize it's iron-plated aluminum.

You buy an American anvil. It's five times the price of the competition, but it comes from a brand that your great-grandfather used to love. It comes boxed with a warranty registration postcard, twenty pages of safety instructions, assay certificate, and a regulatory slip which lists its FCC certification and ITAR registration. It looks just like your friend's KIXJBU. There's a "Made In China" sticker on the bottom.

You buy a Russian anvil. It arrives coated in cosmoline, wrapped in newspaper from 1974, and weighing 40% more than advertised. The finish looks like it was machined with a shovel. The face is not flat, but somehow this does not matter. You drop it off a truck, accidentally leave it outside for six winters, and use it to straighten a bulldozer blade. It's fine.

You buy a Swedish anvil. It comes flat-packed in a long cardboard box with cheerful Neo-Grotesk lettering and a line drawing of a smiling man assembling it with an Allen key. The instructions contain no words, only pictograms showing the anvil face, horn, waist, feet, and 112 identical-looking fasteners. Halfway through assembly, you discover that the pritchel hole was installed upside down, but only because you used peg B17 where you should have used peg B71. Once assembled, it is clean, stable, and works better than it has any right to. You immediately wonder whether you should have bought two.

You buy a Japanese anvil. It arrives wrapped in rice paper inside a paulownia box, accompanied by a certificate bearing three generations of signatures and a photograph of the first production example being presented to the Emperor. The face has been hand-polished by a seventy-eight-year-old master whose family has made striking surfaces since the Muromachi period. You are given detailed instructions for oiling it with a cloth folded in a specific way. It is the most beautiful object you own. You never quite work up the nerve to strike it.","created_at":"Tue May 05 19:22:17 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/dfranke/status/2051744309641191503","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

{"id":"2040075793410187603","author":"jihprobs","name":"jihyun","text":"ive been building something similar for my founder journey and because im extra ✨ i built my own md writing app with embedded terminal (instead of obsidian) all local, WYSIWYG editor and calm UI 🍵 https://t.co/DzPmdVkodo","likes":2,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":218,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Fri Apr 03 14:35:46 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/jihprobs/status/2040075793410187603","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2039805659525644595","author":"karpathy","name":"Andrej Karpathy","text":"LLM Knowledge Bases

Something I'm finding very useful recently: using LLMs to build personal knowledge bases for various topics of research interest. In this way, a large fraction of my recent token throughput is going less into manipulating code, and more into manipulating knowledge (stored as markdown and images). The latest LLMs are quite good at it. So:

Data ingest:
I index source documents (articles, papers, repos, datasets, images, etc.) into a raw/ directory, then I use an LLM to incrementally "compile" a wiki, which is just a collection of .md files in a directory structure. The wiki includes summaries of all the data in raw/, backlinks, and then it categorizes data into concepts, writes articles for them, and links them all. To convert web articles into .md files I like to use the Obsidian Web Clipper extension, and then I also use a hotkey to download all the related images to local so that my LLM can easily reference them.

IDE:
I use Obsidian as the IDE "frontend" where I can view the raw data, the the compiled wiki, and the derived visualizations. Important to note that the LLM writes and maintains all of the data of the wiki, I rarely touch it directly. I've played with a few Obsidian plugins to render and view data in other ways (e.g. Marp for slides).

Q&A:
Where things get interesting is that once your wiki is big enough (e.g. mine on some recent research is ~100 articles and ~400K words), you can ask your LLM agent all kinds of complex questions against the wiki, and it will go off, research the answers, etc. I thought I had to reach for fancy RAG, but the LLM has been pretty good about auto-maintaining index files and brief summaries of all the documents and it reads all the important related data fairly easily at this ~small scale.

Output:
Instead of getting answers in text/terminal, I like to have it render markdown files for me, or slide shows (Marp format), or matplotlib images, all of which I then view again in Obsidian. You can imagine many other visual output formats depending on the query. Often, I end up "filing" the outputs back into the wiki to enhance it for further queries. So my own explorations and queries always "add up" in the knowledge base.

Linting:
I've run some LLM "health checks" over the wiki to e.g. find inconsistent data, impute missing data (with web searchers), find interesting connections for new article candidates, etc., to incrementally clean up the wiki and enhance its overall data integrity. The LLMs are quite good at suggesting further questions to ask and look into.

Extra tools:
I find myself developing additional tools to process the data, e.g. I vibe coded a small and naive search engine over the wiki, which I both use directly (in a web ui), but more often I want to hand it off to an LLM via CLI as a tool for larger queries. 

Further explorations:
As the repo grows, the natural desire is to also think about synthetic data generation + finetuning to have your LLM "know" the data in its weights instead of just context windows.

TLDR: raw data from a given number of sources is collected, then compiled by an LLM into a .md wiki, then operated on by various CLIs by the LLM to do Q&A and to incrementally enhance the wiki, and all of it viewable in Obsidian. You rarely ever write or edit the wiki manually, it's the domain of the LLM. I think there is room here for an incredible new product instead of a hacky collection of scripts.","created_at":"Thu Apr 02 20:42:21 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/karpathy/status/2039805659525644595","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[]}}

If you’ve ever done the math on how long you get with your dog, this one’s for you.

There’s a biomarker called IGF-1 that has a lot to say about how fast they age. It’s a growth hormone from the liver, and smaller dogs naturally run lower — one reason they often get more years.
You don’t need to panic about the number. You just need to know it. From there, the levers are gentle: right-sized portions, steady insulin, less inflammation.
Knowing what’s happening inside is how you make the years count.

"I've used AI, but I don't really trust the output."

We hear this from finance leaders all the time.

They'll get a file. They'll get numbers. But they won't use them because they have no idea how the AI got there.

So finance teams end up validating everything manually anyway. Which defeats the entire point.

Here's what we did differently in Pluvo:

We show you the steps. You can follow the AI through its journey. You see how it got to the answer... not just the answer itself.

If you can't trace it, you can't trust it. And if you can't trust it, you won't use it.

That's why verticalized AI matters. It's not about being smarter, it's about being built for how finance actually works.

evidence.title: The way we interact with technology is fundamentally shifting over the next 5 years. And we're building for where that's headed. Here's what we see coming: Compute is becoming a commodity. It's getting cheaper, faster, more accessible. That's not the differentiator anymore. The new unit of measure isn't compute - it's inference. It's not about how fast you can process data. It's about how well you can turn that data into judgment. Most tools stop at showing you what happened. Systems of judgment help you understand why it happened and what to do next. That's the shift. From systems of record to systems of judgment. We're building Pluvo for how teams will want to make decisions over the next 10-20 years... by preserving context, reasoning, and outcomes in one place. Because the companies that win won't be the ones with the most data or the fastest compute. They'll be the ones with the best judgment.

pluvoapp
The way we interact with technology is fundamentally shifting over the next 5 years.

And we're building for where that's headed.

Here's what we see coming:

Compute is becoming a commodity. It's getting cheaper, faster, more accessible. That's not the differentiator anymore.

The new unit of measure isn't compute - it's inference.

It's not about how fast you can process data. It's about how well you can turn that data into judgment.

Most tools stop at showing you what happened. Systems of judgment help you understand why it happened and what to do next.

That's the shift. From systems of record to systems of judgment.

We're building Pluvo for how teams will want to make decisions over the next 10-20 years... by preserving context, reasoning, and outcomes in one place.

Because the companies that win won't be the ones with the most data or the fastest compute. They'll be the ones with the best judgment.

{"id":"2077148536148500883","author":"jihprobs","name":"jihyun","text":"always be encouraging to your quantized models","likes":2,"retweets":0,"replies":0,"views":169,"is_retweet":false,"created_at":"Tue Jul 14 21:49:37 +0000 2026","url":"https://x.com/jihprobs/status/2077148536148500883","has_media":false,"media_urls":[],"media_posters":[],"quoted_tweet":{"id":"2076469675576459749","author":"CashelFitz","name":"Cashel Fitzgerald","text":"New FAIR paper dropped 🙀: Quantization makes reasoning models more indecisive

Lotfi et al. show that quantized models tend to doubt themselves, more often saying 'wait,' 'but,' or 'alternatively' and talking themselves out of the answer.

Penalizing overthinking at test time leads to a measurable (up to 12-23%) decrease in CoT token usage while maintaining accuracy.

This is why I always prompt inject affirmations into my cua models 😂

“Normal” is the most misleading word on your dog’s lab report.

It reads like an all-clear. It isn’t. The “normal range” is built from a crowd of strangers — different breeds, different ages, different bodies. By design, 5% of perfectly healthy dogs fall outside it. And a result can climb, head the wrong direction, and never leave “normal” at all.

One snapshot against a population that was never built for your dog will always miss what her own baseline would catch.

We broke it down on our Substack. Link in bio 🔗

In the world of high-scale manufacturing, "vision" isn't about dreaming. It’s about transparency.

Most people see a factory as just machines and manpower. But a true leader sees the underlying logic. They see the friction in a process before it becomes a delay. They see a 1% inefficiency and recognize it as a threat to their global competitiveness. To compete at a global level, you must be able to see what your competitors are ignoring.

When you can see the invisible, the impossible becomes achievable. The future belongs to those who see the details others choose to ignore.

evidence.title: One thing CFOs need to stop doing immediately: Spending hours (if not weeks) on excessive financial modeling, building reports, doing journal entries, and paying invoices. You're spending your days in the weeds of manual work when you should be thinking about where to invest and how to grow the business. All of that operational stuff? It can be handed off. Or better yet, automated with the right technology. Your time is the most valuable resource in the business. Full stop. And if you're spending it on tasks that technology can handle, you're not doing the strategic work only you can do. Leverage technology. Automate what you can. Free yourself up to do the work that actually matters. Because the business doesn't need you to be a better data processor. It needs you to be a strategic leader.

evidence.title: Here's what's broken with the current landscape of FP&A tools: Every insight is gatekept by modeling. Before you can get to your first "aha moment", before you can see the answer, understand the variance, or test a scenario... you have to build a model. And modeling is hard. It takes a lot of time to get to the insight you actually need. You spend hours building the structure. Setting up formulas. Linking sheets. Testing assumptions. Debugging errors. And by the time you finally get the model working, the question you were trying to answer might have changed. The insight shouldn't be gatekept by the complexity of the tool. That's why we built Pluvo differently: You can get to insights without having to build models from scratch first. The system understands your data, your structure, and your business context, so you can go straight to the questions that matter. Model when you need to. But don't let modeling block you from making decisions. The best decisions happen fast. The best tools shouldn't slow you down.

AI has been around for a long time. But LLMs changed everything for finance teams.

Here's why:

Finance has always been about taking fragmented data from multiple sources, consolidating it, pivoting it, and turning it into a model you can actually use to make decisions.

That process used to take hours, sometimes days.

LLMs let you talk to your data in natural language. You can ask questions, understand patterns, and build models faster than ever before.

But here's what really matters:

The scorekeeping work—the data gathering, the reconciliations, the manual pivots—can now be automated through agents.

Which means finance leaders can finally focus on what they should have been doing all along:

Helping decision makers make better decisions.

Not collecting data. Not fixing broken formulas. Not chasing down numbers.

Strategic work. Analysis. Judgment.

That's the shift LLMs enable. And it's why the finance function is fundamentally changing.

The teams that figure this out first will have a massive advantage.

evidence.title: Peking duck is one of my favorite dishes, but it has come under the crossfire of tariffs and EU–China trade tensions.
evidence.text: Peking duck is one of my favorite dishes, but it has come under the crossfire of tariffs and EU–China trade tensions. The European Commission has opened an anti-dumping investigation into Chinese Pekin duck meat imports after complaints from five European producers. In what may be a case of "fowl play", the producers allege that Chinese exporters are selling duck meat in the EU at prices that undercut local farms. If the Commission finds evidence of dumping, it can impose duties on the imports. So far, the EU has tended to target industrial products such as chemicals and electric vehicles. China has responded with tariffs on European pork, dairy products, and cognac. The duck investigation takes the dispute further into the food supply chain. Trade tensions between Brussels and Beijing are now affecting not only factories and carmakers, but also farmers, restaurants, and grocery shelves.

I started Coval with the belief that the simulation and evaluation approaches that made autonomous vehicles a reality could unlock the same for voice AI. That parallel has only gotten sharper as enterprises deploy autonomous conversational agents at scale.

Voice and chat are the new interface in the AI era. Talking is the most natural way to interact with complex autonomous systems. The same way web and mobile transformed every enterprise, every company will have a voice agent as the front door to their product. This platform shift is happening now.

From Y Combinator to working with companies like @DeepgramAI, @perplexity_ai , and @Zoom, it's been a wild ride. We watched voice AI go from an emerging modality to every Fortune 500 enterprise building a conversational interface.

Autonomous agents are the future. But you can't ship and hope for the best when agents are taking on real work. The stakes are too high. 

Coval will be what enables us to actually trust those agents. The platform to help teams reliably scale voice and chat agents.

We wouldn’t be here without Coval’s founding engineers @rheacoval and Kobi Hudson. Rhea took a chance on Coval before we had a single customer, a line of code, or an office that wasn't my couch. Kobi left @Waymo after 10 years building foundational simulation systems to help us build the frontier of voice simulation.

To the full Coval team - you all are insane engineers and builders who inspire me every day. Rob Young Alejandra Vergara Henry Finkelstein Callum Reid Dakota Mallen Dana Dzik Mallory McLoughlin Christopher Kuester Jake Levi Brooke Hartley Kappi Patterson

To all our investors - @NorwestVP, @Base10Partners Partners, @twilio Ventures, @ycombinator, @alumniventures, Swift Ventures, Fortitude VC and so many more. You are what made Coval possible.

To @koh_terai who brought my video vision to life.

And last but certainly not least, thank you to everyone who's been building with us.

“Women deserve real data about their bodies, not guesswork,” explain the founders of Clair.

Clair is being touted as the “first continuous hormone tracker” designed to monitor estrogen and progesterone patterns, in real time. 

Using 10 biosensors (tracking everything from skin temperature to heart rate variability and sleep architecture), Clair translates subtle physiological signals into a live picture of your hormonal shifts. The result? Insights that go far beyond step counts and calorie burn.

Because hormones don’t just affect fertility - they shape your energy, mood, sleep, and even how your body responds to exercise.

“For too long, women’s health has relied on methods that haven’t changed in decades. Peeing on sticks, taking temperatures at 5 am, painful needles and microneedles, tracking symptoms after the fact. Too many women get dismissed with “It’s just your cycle” when something is genuinely wrong, because they lack the evidence to prove otherwise,” Founders Jenny and Abhinav explain.

Clair can confirm ovulation (not just predict it), explain why you feel exhausted despite “perfect” recovery scores, and even help athletes understand why some workouts feel effortless one week… and impossible the next.

It’s also stepping into a space that’s long been underserved: perimenopause and menopause, where many women are left navigating major changes with very little data or clarity.

Until now, hormone tracking has lived at two extremes - invasive and expensive (clinical blood tests), or manual and inconsistent (at-home kits). Clair sits in the middle, making it continuous, passive, and wearable.

Women’s health tech has been playing catch-up for years.

This might be what catching up finally looks like.

evidence.title: 📌 AI x 設計美學 未來創業 × 超現實主題視覺 夢想與科技交錯，營造啟發與思辨並存的氛圍 這張以「AI × 少年 × 創業未來」為主題的視覺作品，透過 象徵式構圖 + 超現實畫面 + 對比文字設計，傳達了科技時代下的新一代創造者精神。 🎨 設計亮點 - 主題構圖：中央高塔象徵「目標與引導」，兩側的宇宙通道象徵「無限可能」與「多維未來」，形成強烈的中心視覺焦點。 - 色彩層次：天空藍 × 金黃色田野 × 深藍宇宙形成三層對比，既現實又夢幻，呈現「理性與想像力並行」的氛圍。 - 人物視角：低視角的人物背影象徵探索與啟程，強化觀者的代入感與未來感。 💡 行銷啟示 科技品牌與創業內容的設計核心在於「啟發性 × 前瞻性」。這張作品以藝術化手法詮釋 AI 未來敘事，不是單純的科技展示，而是一場對「人與 AI 共創未來」的提問，非常適合用於思想品牌、創業論壇、或未來趨勢系列。 📲 想看更多品牌設計靈感？Follow 我們，每週帶你拆解一張好設計！ #AIx設計美學 #未來創業 #AIAgent #品牌視覺 #品牌設計靈感 #視覺行銷 #行銷美學 #設計靈感 #廣告設計解析 #商業設計 #品牌塑造 #設計美感 #未來主義 #科技藝術 #創業靈感 See translation

evidence.title: CFOs: here's why AI in finance still makes you nervous. You need numbers you can defend in a board meeting. You need to show your work. You need to know exactly how you got from A to B. And most AI gives you a black box. The solution is to make sure AI stays in its own lane. There are things it shouldn't touch. Let AI handle context. Let it surface explanations, identify patterns, and write narratives about what's happening in your business. That's where it excels. But keep the math deterministic. If you put numbers in, you should get the same numbers out every time- no hallucinations or probabilistic drift in your P&L. When you separate reasoning from calculation, you get the best of both worlds: AI that makes you faster without making you nervous.

CFOs: here's why AI in finance still makes you nervous.

You need numbers you can defend in a board meeting. You need to show your work. You need to know exactly how you got from A to B.

And most AI gives you a black box.

The solution is to make sure AI stays in its own lane. There are things it shouldn't touch.

Let AI handle context. Let it surface explanations, identify patterns, and write narratives about what's happening in your business. That's where it excels.

But keep the math deterministic. If you put numbers in, you should get the same numbers out every time- no hallucinations or probabilistic drift in your P&L.

When you separate reasoning from calculation, you get the best of both worlds:

AI that makes you faster without making you nervous.

evidence.title: We keep hearing the same thing from finance teams: "I'm not worried about speed. I'm worried about trust." A Director of FP&A at a $230M ARR company told us that generating reports faster was a low priority. Their biggest concern was validating that the data feeding those reports was actually correct. They spend hours each week reconciling: - QuickBooks vs. Salesforce revenue numbers - HubSpot pipeline vs. financial forecast - Payroll system vs. budget headcount - Stripe transactions vs. accounting records The data exists in five different places with five different definitions of "customer," "revenue," and "closed deal." Every variance triggers a hunt: Is this a real business change or a data mismatch? Did revenue actually drop or did someone change how we categorize subscriptions? Finance teams end up being data detectives instead of strategic advisors. This is why AI tools that just "generate insights faster" miss the point. Speed without validation is just faster wrong answers. What teams actually need: connected systems where the logic is traceable, the calculations are auditable, and when numbers don't match, you can see exactly why. The analysis should show its work.

We keep hearing the same thing from finance teams: "I'm not worried about speed. I'm worried about trust."

A Director of FP&A at a $230M ARR company told us that generating reports faster was a low priority. Their biggest concern was validating that the data feeding those reports was actually correct.

They spend hours each week reconciling:

- QuickBooks vs. Salesforce revenue numbers
- HubSpot pipeline vs. financial forecast
- Payroll system vs. budget headcount
- Stripe transactions vs. accounting records

The data exists in five different places with five different definitions of "customer," "revenue," and "closed deal."

Every variance triggers a hunt: Is this a real business change or a data mismatch? Did revenue actually drop or did someone change how we categorize subscriptions?

Finance teams end up being data detectives instead of strategic advisors.

This is why AI tools that just "generate insights faster" miss the point. Speed without validation is just faster wrong answers.

What teams actually need: connected systems where the logic is traceable, the calculations are auditable, and when numbers don't match, you can see exactly why.

The analysis should show its work.

evidence.title: 📌 AI x 設計美學 物理治療 × 專業健康視覺 疼痛緩解 × 機能恢復，營造專業與信任兼備的品牌形象 這張五十肩物理治療宣傳圖，以 主題人物痛點表現 + 對比療效展示 + 專業資訊分區 的構圖，清楚傳達療程功效與品牌專業感。 🎨 設計亮點 - 主標題設計：「告別50肩，抬手不再卡住」以大字體強調痛點與成果對比，立即吸睛 - 視覺焦點：主角抓著肩膀皺眉的表情，明確傳達「疼痛感」；下方對比區塊展示「放鬆」與「舉手順暢」，視覺對比清晰 - 色彩基調：綠色 × 藍青色調象徵健康與修復，搭配局部黃色強調優惠與 CTA - 資訊分區：以「筋膜放鬆、消炎止痛」為兩大重點效果，配合人體結構圖與真實照片，兼具專業與真實感 - 信任標語：非入侵綜合理療、聚焦衝擊波、電磁波等關鍵技術詞彙，增強專業可信度 💡 行銷啟示 醫療健康類設計的核心在於「痛點直擊 + 專業信任」。這張圖透過動態表情、清晰療效對比和明確療程技術，讓受眾直觀感受到「這個療法真的有用」，有效促進諮詢與預約。 📲 想看更多品牌設計靈感？Follow 我地，帶你拆解一張好設計！ #AIx設計美學 #物理治療 #肩周炎 #五十肩 #健康設計 #品牌視覺 #品牌設計靈感 #視覺行銷 #行銷美學 #設計靈感 #廣告設計解析 #商業設計 #品牌塑造 #設計美感 #健康品牌 #治療推廣 #疼痛管理 See translation

evidence.title: HBR published a piece in 2019 on why sales teams struggle with forecasting accuracy. The diagnosis: human behaviour, not algorithms. Salespeople withhold bad news, keep two sets of books, and cling to optimistic beliefs about troubled deals. The solutions focused on behaviour - track deal progress continuously, focus on deal age, detect who's gaming the system. Seven years later, we're hearing a different problem from the field. A consultant who works with PE-backed companies told us her top requirement is model flexibility. Her clients constantly change how they analyze revenue - this quarter by customer segment, next quarter by acquisition channel, then by cohort when the board asks new questions. The human behaviour problems haven't gone away. But now there's a tooling problem too. Most FP&A systems assume you'll set up your model once. But growing businesses change how they track revenue quarter to quarter. When your tool can't adapt, finance teams resort to exactly the behaviours HBR warned about: keeping two sets of books. One in the rigid system, one in Excel where they can actually model the business. The 2019 problems still exist. But now we're adding tool rigidity on top of human behaviour. What's changed about how you forecast in the past five years?

HBR published a piece in 2019 on why sales teams struggle with forecasting accuracy.

The diagnosis: human behaviour, not algorithms. Salespeople withhold bad news, keep two sets of books, and cling to optimistic beliefs about troubled deals.

The solutions focused on behaviour - track deal progress continuously, focus on deal age, detect who's gaming the system.

Seven years later, we're hearing a different problem from the field.

A consultant who works with PE-backed companies told us her top requirement is model flexibility. Her clients constantly change how they analyze revenue - this quarter by customer segment, next quarter by acquisition channel, then by cohort when the board asks new questions.

The human behaviour problems haven't gone away. But now there's a tooling problem too.

Most FP&A systems assume you'll set up your model once. But growing businesses change how they track revenue quarter to quarter.

When your tool can't adapt, finance teams resort to exactly the behaviours HBR warned about: keeping two sets of books. One in the rigid system, one in Excel where they can actually model the business.

The 2019 problems still exist. But now we're adding tool rigidity on top of human behaviour.

What's changed about how you forecast in the past five years?

evidence.title: 📌 AI x 設計美學 中醫療程 × 溫潤自然視覺 產後護理 × 髮根重建，營造專業與關懷並存的品牌氛圍 這張中醫養髮宣傳圖，以 分區對比 + 插圖說明 + 暖色調設計 的方式呈現，讓觀者迅速理解「產後脫髮成因」與「治療方向」，整體兼具專業可信與溫柔照護感。 🎨 設計亮點 - 標題層級：「產後掉髮不是自然現象」以深棕描邊字強調警示感；副標「體虛型脫髮更難自癒」延伸問題深度 - 人物對比照：左側「脫髮焦慮」、右側「掉髮困擾」，情緒代入感強，建立共鳴 - 底部資訊分區：以三個圖示說明療程核心（補氣養血、調理脾腎、針灸疏通），結構簡潔、專業易懂 - 色彩基調：以米棕、杏膚與暖木紋為主，呼應「自然中醫 × 健康修復」的品牌調性 💡 行銷啟示 健康療程類設計的關鍵在於「專業可信 + 情緒共鳴」。這張圖以真實人物焦慮表情搭配中醫圖示概念，讓受眾立即產生信任感與需求感，是兼具教育與轉化力的高效組合。 📲 想看更多品牌設計靈感？Follow 我地，帶你拆解好設計！ #AIx設計美學 #中醫養髮 #產後脫髮 #品牌視覺 #品牌設計靈感 #視覺行銷 #行銷美學 #設計靈感 #廣告設計解析 #商業設計 #品牌塑造 #設計美感 #健康養生 #氣血調理 #脾腎調理 #針灸治療 #女性健康 See translation

evidence.title: 📌 AI x 設計美學 汽車品牌 × 情境式防災視覺 暴雨風球 × 出車貼士，營造專業與信任兼具的品牌形象 這張宣傳圖以 真實天氣場景 + 情境式文案 + 溫馨提醒布局 呈現，成功把「品牌專業」與「顧客關懷」結合成具信任感的行銷素材。 🎨 設計亮點 - 主題設計：「遇上暴雨風球 點算好？」以大字白字配深色雨景背景，強烈對比下瞬間抓住眼球 - 場景氛圍：真實雨天車輛實拍，雨滴與濕地反光讓畫面具臨場感，傳遞「實戰應用」氛圍 - 配色基調：深灰 × 墨綠 × 黃色強調標籤，呈現穩重又醒目的品牌語調 - 資訊結構：分為兩大模組——「出車安排」與「溫馨貼士」，用直線分隔條保持視覺秩序 💡 行銷啟示 汽車品牌內容行銷的關鍵在於「功能之外的信任連結」。這張圖透過天氣應變情境教育，巧妙轉化為品牌責任與專業象徵，在建立信任的同時，也潛移默化強化品牌記憶度。 📲 想看更多品牌設計靈感？Follow 我們，每週帶你拆解一張好設計！ #AIx設計美學 #汽車品牌 #暴雨風球 #品牌視覺 #行銷美學 #品牌設計靈感 #視覺行銷 #設計靈感 #廣告設計解析 #商業設計 #品牌塑造 #設計美感 #汽車安全 #情境行銷 #AutoBright See translation

@clair_health is decoding women’s well-being.

The wearable maker secured $11.6M ahead of launching its continuous hormone monitor in November.

The device uses 10 biosensors and 130+ proprietary biomarkers to track hormones including estrogen, progesterone, LH, and FSH, helping women better understand fertility, performance, recovery, and menopause.

Already attracting 25K+ people to its waitlist, Clair is building a new category of wearable focused on hormonal health across every life stage.

Rather than adding women’s health as a feature, Clair is building a wearable with hormones at its core.

Your U.S. entity files April 15. Your Canadian entity files April 30.

Your accountant needs the numbers a week before each deadline. Your ERP has one set of books. Your spreadsheet has another. And someone on the finance team is spending their evenings reconciling the two.

Multi-entity tax season is where the cracks in your financial infrastructure show up all at once. The messy chart of accounts you've been meaning to fix. The intercompany transactions nobody categorized properly. The Q4 adjustment that got made in the spreadsheet but not in the system.

We built Pluvo for the other 11 months of the year. But every April, our clients remind us why having a clean, connected financial picture matters year-round: because the teams who have it are finishing their filings right now. The ones who don't are rebuilding their books from scratch.

Wishing calm nerves and clean reconciliations to every finance team in the middle of it.

Happy filing season ☔

Squeezed in a selfie with Garry Tan, Paul Graham, and Jessica Livingston at YC! 📸😁

Growing up, I used to read Paul Graham’s essays like they were scripture.

I watched every YC talk on YouTube. Read everything I could find about how he and Jessica built it from nothing. Two people who just believed the best founders were out there, overlooked, underestimated, and decided to bet on them anyway.

They shaped how I think. How I build. How I see the world.

This week, they came to YC to give a talk.

And I was sitting in the room.

After years of reading the words on a screen, I got to hear it in person. The early days. The doubt. The sheer amount of hardwork behind everything that looks inevitable in hindsight.

It reminded me that nothing starts polished. Everything great starts somewhere small and uncertain and a little scary.

We are 8 days from Demo Day. @saudara.ai let's goo! 🚀

Somewhere became here.

evidence.title: Our last video wasn't our best work, and we knew we could do better. So at 11 PM, we called a friend. By 6 AM the next morning, he was on a flight. Sometimes the only way to make something you're proud of is to move fast and figure it out as you go. Opened a jar. Folded a shirt. Swept a floor. Your hands knew the whole sequence before your brain got involved.

None of it was ever written down. There is no tutorial, no dataset, no archive of how a real person moves through a real home. Which is exactly why robots stall the moment they leave a lab.

Hub pays people to film those ordinary tasks, first person, inside their own homes. Free head strap, no schedule, no experience needed. Every hour that clears review is paid.

Swipe for how it works.

Send this to someone who thinks robots are further along than they are.

Excited to finally share: after five years as a scientist, I’ve left my corporate job to build a startup full-time with my dream co-founder!
From modeling to PhD in CS, to working in big tech, and now starting a startup—my career path has been unexpected but fulfilling.
This decision wasn’t made lightly. Leaving stability is scary, but I’m grateful for the incredible support and advice from so many. We can’t wait to share what we’re building.
More updates soon 🤍
個人近況更新：在矽谷科技公司待了五年以後，我正式離職、開始創業了！而且和我一起合夥的是一個我一直很景仰的超酷女生！
從小時候做模特、到跑來美國念資工博士、到在矽谷當科學家、然後現在要開始做自己的科技新創。這條路走得不太像我年輕的時候想像的樣子，但是能說是比我夢想中的樣子還好。

Excited to finally share: after five years as a scientist, I’ve left my corporate job to build a startup full-time with my dream co-founder!

From modeling to PhD in CS, to working in big tech, and now starting a startup—my career path has been unexpected but fulfilling.

This decision wasn’t made lightly. Leaving stability is scary, but I’m grateful for the incredible support and advice from so many. We can’t wait to share what we’re building.

More updates soon 🤍

個人近況更新：在矽谷科技公司待了五年以後，我正式離職、開始創業了！而且和我一起合夥的是一個我一直很景仰的超酷女生！

從小時候做模特、到跑來美國念資工博士、到在矽谷當科學家、然後現在要開始做自己的科技新創。這條路走得不太像我年輕的時候想像的樣子，但是能說是比我夢想中的樣子還好。

花了很多時間和自我糾結才做下這個決定。在大公司待久了，下定決心要離開舒服的日子其實真的滿恐怖。非常感謝過去這些日子身邊每個聽我講創業講到不行的親朋好友們。我最近應該很無聊因為開口閉口就是同一個話題。謝謝大家的鼓勵和支持，還有好多好多超寶貴意見！
